news.title: Boasting Trump Shamed by Camera Showing Empty Seats
news.text:
Donald Trump’s boast about the crowd size at his Texas rally on Wednesday got promptly exposed by a C-SPAN camera showing dozens of empty seats. 

Trump, 80, spoke at San Antonio’s Freeman Coliseum to support Senate candidate Ken Paxon. During a moment in his speech when he wasn’t interrupted by protesters, the audience-obsessed president couldn’t help but insist that he filled up the arena, despite evidence to the contrary.

“Look at this place. Every corner. They will say they spotted an empty seat,” he said, referring to the press. “You know, there are lines that are two miles long outside. They can’t get in.” 

That claim could not be immediately verified.

“I tell people, ‘please, please do not leave, do not go to the bathroom, because the fake news will take a picture of two empty seats and they’ll say Trump did not fill up’—who the hell fills up an arena like this for a midterm?” he claimed.

At that moment, the camera panned across the arena’s upper section, which revealed dozens of empty seats.

Trump maintained that there were enough people to fill those seats in the arena—they were just elsewhere.

“And what they do is in the upper rows, you’ll see it, they sort of migrate downward, and they all stay [indecipherable],” he said. “We max out everything that you‘ve ever seen. There‘s never been anything like it.”

But, as the Daily Beast has noted, Trump’s rallies have generally not been the draw they used to be. Just last week, the president’s visit to deep-red Mobile, Alabama, saw empty row upon empty row in the upper deck. Local media reported that that arena, built for around 10,000 people, saw around 8,000 rallygoers.

When that fact was reported, Trump flipped out, insisting in a Truth Social post that the venue had been “MAXED OUT.” 

Not only that, he argued, but his events “for very good Republican Politicians are probably more crowded than ever.”

The White House did not immediately respond to a request for comment about his Wednesday rally. 

During it, one of the president’s supporters attacked a protester who disrupted his speech, pulling him toward the ground by his hair. Other Trump supporters stepped in to pull him away.

“Let me ask you something: is there anything like a Trump rally?” an enthused Trump said afterward. “I don’t think so.”

news.title: After botched US execution, Christa Pike was nearly taken off life support
news.text:
Washington: A convicted US killer who survived a botched execution was almost taken off life support before she regained consciousness, her lawyer said Wednesday, as a court ordered prison authorities to preserve evidence in the case.

One week after Christa Pike survived her execution by lethal injection, the state of Texas carried out the execution of a 46-year-old man using the same method.

Pike, 50, who was sentenced to death for a murder she committed when she was a teenager, received two supposedly lethal doses of the drug pentobarbital at a Tennessee prison last Wednesday.

She survived the injections, however, and was rushed to a hospital where she was in critical condition for several days, unconscious and on a ventilator.

“On Monday night, it was our understanding that Christa was brain dead, and that life support would be removed the next day,” her lawyer Randy Spivey told reporters.

“But on Tuesday, to the shock of everyone...Christa woke up and began talking.”

Pike remains shackled to her hospital bed, awake and able to speak a little but incapable of swallowing or moving her arms, according to her attorneys.

“I think she is angry and confused about everything right now,” Spivey said, adding: “She is very aware of what they did to her — up to a point.”

“She cannot move either of her arms, both of her arms and hands are tremendously swollen, and we do not know what, if any, function she will regain in her arms,” he continued, adding that “there’s a long road ahead” for her recovery.

“Medical staff have asked that the shackles be removed and have been denied that request,” Pike’s lawyer Luke Ihnen said at a court hearing.

An anesthesiologist retained by Pike’s lawyers as an expert ahead of her execution told the BBC that she was off the ventilator.

She has “no memory, I believe, of the execution attempt,” Joel Zivot said, adding that Pike knows her name and thinks it is currently September.

“We have to ask how much suffering is enough? We continue to ask (Tennessee Governor Bill Lee) to commute Christa’s death sentence” to life in prison, Spivey said.

The court ordered state corrections officials to preserve all evidence related to the botched execution including medical supplies, waste, and audio and video recordings.

Pike’s fate revived debate over capital punishment in the United States.

Lee suspended executions in Tennessee pending an independent investigation and the state’s prison chief resigned. Tennessee’s correction department has maintained that it followed established protocol.

The state of Texas carried out an execution by lethal injection later Wednesday, the first in the United States since the attempt to put Pike to death.

Jamaal Howard was sentenced to death for killing a store clerk during a 2000 robbery.

His lawyers had sought to have his execution postponed, citing Pike’s case, but he was pronounced dead at 8:03 p.m. local time (0103 GMT Thursday).

“I’m sorry for what happened, I wish you could learn to forgive me one of these days,” Howard said in his last statement before being put to death.

First to survive 

The Death Penalty Information Center, which publishes data and analysis on capital punishment in the United States, said Pike was the first inmate to survive after being injected with lethal doses of execution drugs.

Pike was 18 when she and her boyfriend beat and killed 19-year-old Colleen Slemmer at a job training camp.

Pike would have been the first woman put to death by the state of Tennessee in more than 200 years, according to the Death Penalty Information Center.

Excluding Pike’s failed execution, there have been 29 executions in the United States this year, which have all been carried out by lethal injection.

The death penalty has been abolished in 23 of the 50 US states, while three others — California, Oregon and Pennsylvania — have moratoriums in place.

The Pentagon said on Monday that President Donald Trump has approved the execution of Nidal Hasan, a US Army psychiatrist who shot dead 13 people and wounded more than two dozen at Fort Hood in Texas in 2009.

Hasan’s execution by firing squad, set for December 3, would be the first carried out by the US military since 1961.
news.summary: Christa Pike, a convicted killer, regained consciousness after a failed execution and was nearly removed from life support. A court has ordered the preservation of evidence in her case.

news.title: Trump announced a phone conversation with Putin
news.text:
There is still no clarity on exactly when the conversation between the presidents of Russia and the United States, Vladimir Putin and Donald Trump, may take place. This was reported to TASS by Dmitry Peskov, the press secretary of the Russian leader.

Answering journalists' question about whether the conversation has already been agreed upon with the Russian side and if there is an understanding of when it might happen, he said: «Not yet. We will inform you.»

The day before, on October 7, Trump announced a phone conversation with the Russian president. «I've agreed to a call. Today is his birthday. Today is Vladimir Putin's birthday. I'm sure you're going to mark it,» he told reporters.

The last time the heads of state spoke on the phone was on September 8. The conversation took place after the visit of American negotiators Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner to Moscow and Kyiv.

news.title: Donald Trump Renews Nobel Peace Prize Bid, Says He Deserves 2026 Award After ‘Settling 8 Wars’ (Video)
news.text:
US President Donald Trump has renewed his push for the 2026 Nobel Peace Prize, saying he believes he deserves the prestigious award but expressing doubts that the Norwegian Nobel Committee will select him. His remarks came just two days before the committee is scheduled to announce this year's laureate on October 9.

Trump Says He Has Settled Eight Wars

Speaking to reporters in the Oval Office on Wednesday, Trump claimed that he had settled eight wars since returning to the White House and had accomplished things no previous US president had achieved.

Trump has repeatedly cited his involvement in international conflicts as evidence that he deserves the Nobel Peace Prize. He has claimed credit for efforts involving conflicts and disputes including Israel-Hamas, Israel-Iran, India-Pakistan, Armenia-Azerbaijan and Cambodia-Thailand. Donald Trump Confuses India With Brazil, Claims 125 Million Voted in ‘Indian Presidential Election’.

Donald Trump Renews Nobel Peace Prize Bid

Trump: "There's never been anybody in the history of the Nobel Prize that deserves it more. I settled eight wars. I stopped the total obliteration of the world." https://t.co/QuDSg52Wac
— Aaron Rupar (@atrupar) October 7, 2026

However, several of these claims have been disputed or remain unresolved. India, for instance, has rejected Trump's assertions that the US played a role in brokering the India-Pakistan ceasefire, saying there was no third-party mediation.

Trump Doubts Nobel Committee Will Honour Him

Despite his renewed appeal for the award, Trump acknowledged that he was not confident about his chances. He said the Nobel Committee had a reputation for possibly not awarding the prize to people like him. Trump also argued that failing to recognise his claimed peace efforts would discredit the committee. His comments came as the Norwegian Nobel Committee prepares to announce the 2026 Nobel Peace Prize on Friday.

Trump Has Reportedly Been Nominated for 2026 Nobel Peace Prize

Trump is among the people reported to have been nominated for this year's Nobel Peace Prize. Leaders from Cambodia, Israel and Pakistan have publicly said they nominated him, although individual nominations cannot be officially verified because the Norwegian Nobel Committee keeps nomination information confidential for 50 years. The committee said 287 candidates were nominated for the 2026 Peace Prize, including 208 individuals and 79 organisations. The winner will be announced on October 9 in Oslo. US Military Finalises Iran Strike Preparations As Donald Trump Weighs Pre-Election Timing.

Trump’s Nobel Prospects Face Questions

Trump's chances of winning the prize remain uncertain, with experts reportedly viewing his prospects as weak. His ongoing conflict with Iran and the lack of a resolution to the Russia-Ukraine war have emerged as major factors in assessments of his candidacy. The president had promised during his campaign to end the Ukraine war, but a settlement has not been reached. Meanwhile, US-Israel military action involving Iran has continued to affect regional security and global energy markets.

María Corina Machado’s Nobel Medal Gesture

Trump has also pointed to an unusual connection with last year's Nobel Peace Prize. Venezuelan opposition leader María Corina Machado, who won the 2025 Nobel Peace Prize, gave her medal to Trump in January 2026. The Norwegian Nobel Committee subsequently clarified that a Nobel Prize cannot be revoked, shared or transferred, meaning Machado's award remained hers despite the gesture.

When Will the 2026 Nobel Peace Prize Be Announced?

The 2026 Nobel Peace Prize will be announced on October 9, with the award ceremony scheduled for December 10 in Oslo. The secretive nature of the nomination process means the identities of the official nominees will not be publicly confirmed for decades. Other names and organisations discussed as potential contenders include Pope Leo, the International Criminal Court, Save the Children and Sudan's Emergency Response Rooms.

(The above story first appeared on LatestLY on Oct 08, 2026 09:39 AM IST. For more news and updates on politics, world, sports, entertainment and lifestyle, log on to our website latestly.com).

His remarks came just two days before the committee is scheduled to announce this year's laureate on October 9.

news.title: EU sends envoy to Beijing as rising exports from China raise economic anxiety
news.text:
The European Union is bracing for a confrontation with China as a trade deficit exceeding $1 billion a day heightens anxiety over potential job losses and pushes the bloc’s political leaders to take a more aggressive approach toward its second-largest trading partner.

The European Commission’s top trade envoy, Maroš Šefčovič, will be in Beijing Thursday for a two-day meeting with Chinese Commerce Minister Wang Wentao. The goal is narrowing the EU’s 360 billion euro ($410 billion) trade deficit with China. Earlier this year, he gave Beijing a deadline of October to provide meaningful results in doing so. 

Politicians and economists across the 27-nation bloc consider China’s massive subsidies and exports a major threat to core industrial sectors from steel foundries to car factories. China diverted many of its exports to the EU and other markets after the U.S. raised tariffs. 

In a debate Tuesday in European Parliament in Strasbourg, lawmakers overwhelmingly expressed anxiety alongside defiance over trade with China. On Wednesday, they voted 454 to 86 on a resolution to toughen up on China that centered on a call for “economic reciprocity and a proportionate EU response if China does not open its markets.”

Ahead of the vote, Hilde Vautmans, the Belgian lawmaker who led the resolution, said that “Europe has economic power, it’s time we used it.”

 EU options range from tariffs to a “trade bazooka” 

Despite the seeming European unity this week, it remains unclear what the EU can or is willing to do. It has already rolled out trade measures against Chinese steel imports and e-commerce small parcels.

France’s High Commission for Strategy and Planning in February called for swift action, like 30% tariffs on many of China’s exports, and a devaluation of the euro against the Chinese currency. Sales of German autos are plummeting in China, but China is also poised to gobble up market share in Europe by undercutting European automakers on price thanks to heavy state subsidies. There have already been mass layoffs at major manufacturers like Volkswagen.

A letter by France and Germany, a copy of which was seen by The Associated Press, called for a sweeping rethink of the EU’s China policy. Among other actions, it proposed making it easier for the European Commission to use the bloc’s so-called “trade bazooka,” the Anti-Coercion Instrument. This is a never-used-before raft of measures for blocking or restricting trade and investment from countries found to be putting undue pressure on EU member nations or corporations.

Yet not all EU nations agree on such tough measures. Spain, the eurozone’s fourth-largest economy, has been less adversarial toward China in recent years. Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez has visited Beijing four times in three years. 

The European Policy Centre in Brussels said in June that European battery producers, solar panels, steel, electric vehicles, chemicals and machinery are already hemorrhaging jobs and capacity and called for a trade investigative body modelled on Section 301 of the U.S. Trade Act.

European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen called the phenomenon another “ China shock ” for Europe, similar to what happened in the U.S. in the early 2000s when hundreds of thousands of factory jobs in the American heartland were wiped out. 

The EU’s ailing economy requires both a domestic overhaul and a more aggressive foreign trade policy, especially with China, said Tim Rühlig, a China analyst at the European Union Institute for Security Studies, the bloc’s internal think tank.

Rühlig also said that European businesses and political leadership bear some blame. 

“It’s clear that just protecting yourself from China is not the future,” Rühlig said. “But to have a chance of making yourself ready for future technologies and to remain competitive in the coming 15-20 years, you have to protect yourself.”

It is impossible to disengage completely with China as the EU did with Russia following its invasion of Ukraine, Rühlig said, but there is robust momentum now to reset trade relations with Beijing.

“Where do we make ourselves independent or at least more diverse? And where do we still work with the Chinese?” Rühlig asked.

 China is ready for a long trade dispute 

This week in Beijing, when asked about the letter penned by France and Germany, a spokesperson at China’s Ministry of Commerce said that the countries should refrain from encouraging the EU to resort to protectionist measures. 

“Protectionism cannot enhance competitiveness, and decoupling or cutting off supply chains will only harm others without benefiting oneself,” the commerce ministry said in a statement.

China is the EU’s second-largest goods trading partner after the U.S., according to European Commission data. Chinese exports to the EU rose 15.3% in the first eight months of this year, according to China’s customs agency, while its imports from the EU rose 6.2%.

“The EU does not have the capacity to wage a trade war against China,” read an editorial last month in China’s state-run Global Times newspaper. “If it is truly determined to do so, then let it try.”

China’s exports to Europe, as well as Southeast Asia, Latin America and Africa, expanded after U.S. tariffs went into effect last year, but it still booked a $1.2 trillion trade surplus globally in 2025. So far, China’s export machine has remained remarkably resilient despite U.S. tariffs and other trade restrictions, said Max Zenglein, Asia Pacific senior economist at The Conference Board.

This past weekend, ahead of the meeting between Šefčovič and Wang, China launched an anti-dumping probe on EU exports of p-nitrotoluene, which is used in dyes and pharmaceuticals. The probe was initiated after Beijing warned last month that it would take retaliatory actions if the EU instituted tougher protectionist trade measures.

“China has been battle-tested by successive rounds of external pressure and, so far, has largely stared down attempts to force a change in course,” said Zenglein.

China’s economy has been largely driven by exports as domestic demand remains sluggish. The EU imports sizable amounts of Chinese lithium-ion batteries and hybrid electric vehicles, and Chinese carmakers are also expanding production capacity in Europe.

While China’s trade surplus has intensified concerns among its major trading partners, trade ties between the U.S. and China appear relatively stable following a summit between Chinese President Xi Jinping and President Donald Trump in Washington, wrote Bank of America economists, turning the attention to China-EU relations.

When it comes to negotiations with the EU, Chinese investment in Europe is likely to be among Beijing’s bargaining chips, Zenglein added, particularly as EU member states compete to attract capital, jobs, and new manufacturing projects.

Chan reported from Hong Kong.
news.summary: The European Union is bracing for a confrontation with China as a trade deficit exceeding $1 billion a day heightens anxiety over potential job losses and pushes the bloc’s political leaders to take a more aggressive approach toward its second-largest trading partner

news.title: The 2028 Race Is About to Start and JD Vance Has Already Won (Probably)
news.text:
We’ve still got the midterms to get through, so maybe it’s too early to talk about the 2028 presidential primary, but then again, why not? After all, the second that 2026 is decided, the 2028 cycle begins. It’s inevitable. Heck, it’s already happening. You can see politicians jostling for position, lofting trial balloons, and generally demonstrating how they are utterly overcome by delusion.

Here’s the fact: the nominee is going to be JD Vance unless either JD Vance or Donald Trump decides it’s not going to be JD Vance.

No debate. There’s no actual contest. That’s how it’s going to work out. That’s the only way it can work out. Anybody telling you anything else is wrong. They may be wrong because they’re crazy. They may be wrong because they’re dumb. They may be wrong because they’re delusional. Maybe they’re wrong and know they’re wrong but are saying it anyway because they think it’s to their advantage. But the truth is indisputable. Donald Trump is going to pick the next Republican nominee, and right now it’s JD Vance.

Now, of course, JD Vance might decide not to do it. He’s got a young and growing family, and his wife might not want to put up with this insanity. She might not want to live with a husband who is in the sights of every leftist sociopath out there with a gun and a grudge. They want to murder us, which we can tell by the fact that they have murdered us in the past and would’ve had a higher body count if they could shoot straight.

Alternatively, JD Vance might not think that 2028 is a great opportunity for Republicans. He’s young, and he’ll have many chances down the road, potentially. There’s always the chance that 2028 is his peak, and that somebody else will come along to grab the spotlight, but he might want to take a bye if things aren’t looking great and the administration is unpopular. But the thing is that things probably will look great.

Oh, if the Democrats take one or both houses of Congress, that’s going to be a mess, but that’s not going to reflect on Trump. That’s going to reflect on the Democrats. You’ll have a ravenous, roiling cauldron of left-wing insanity, weirdness, and perversion going on every single day, which will serve to remind people of what the alternative to sober, successful Republican rule is. In 2026, they’re doing everything they can not to remind people what they will do once they get power again. They won’t be able to hide it once they have a little; they’ve already promised to do nothing but investigate political enemies and try to impeach Trump. After the third, fourth, or even fifth impeachment, people are going to get a little tired of that nonsense. Political onanism only goes so far.

But the bigger problem for the Democrats is that Trump’s economy is going to start kicking in over the next year. The new golden age got delayed by trouble with the Fed and with the Iran war, but the economy is fundamentally sound and improving. Things are going to start rocking. We’ve seen this before, those of us who aren’t 12. Remember 1982? The great Ronald Reagan got crushed in the 1982 midterms because his economic policies hadn’t kicked in yet. But by 1984, they had, and it was morning in America, buddy. Reagan won every state except Minnesota, and the way Minnesota is going, that might be up for grabs in 2028, too.

Also, the Iran war is going to be finished by 2028, while Cuba’s going to be free; communists will be swinging from the lampposts — that’s Marco Rubio’s consolation prize for skipping the 2028 cycle. The problem for the Democrats is all they can do is stop legislation and complain. Trump’s going to get the credit for the economy, and the Democrats will have a track record of opposing everything that led to the golden age. And that means the next Republicans are going to have a solid opportunity in 2028, particularly if the Democrats nominate Kamala Harris, and what are the chances of them picking a creepy white sociopath like Gavin Newsom over a black communist woman?

I don’t think JD will let this opportunity go, and unless he gets in a big fight with Donald Trump — always a possibility — Donald Trump will anoint him, and most everyone in the GOP will fall in line.

But what about the guys who won’t? What about the guys who, despite JD's inevitability, throw their hat in the ring?

There would be two main kinds of competing primary opponents, the bitter and the delusional. Start with the bitter. These are the guys who’ve been rejected. These are the guys who’ve presented themselves to Republican voters and been soundly rejected. They’re terrible. They just don’t fit where we are, and it makes them mad that the peasants are revolting. How dare the proles not recognize their manifest superiority and entitlement to greater glory!

There are a bunch of these malcontents out there. I’m sure we’ll see Mike Pence give it another whirl; he’s the party guest who doesn’t know when to leave, except he doesn’t drink, so he didn’t even provide the entertainment that a drunk would. How about Don Bacon, that guy from Nebraska? He was an Air Force general, which says everything you need to know; rarely do you meet anyone else who is simultaneously so pleased with himself and so bereft of any reason to be a general officer jumping into politics. He’s pretty sure that the GOP needs amnesty and submission, but no one’s biting at that bait. That’s why he didn’t bother running again in his blue-leaning district; it wasn’t the Democrat votes he was worried about earning.

And then there are guys like Thomas Massie, the herpes of American politics — he’s gross and never goes away. He does speak for a constituency, though, the geniuses who are convinced there’s a giant Epstein conspiracy out there somewhere that Tommyboy will someday disclose — someday—and who also blame Jews for their inability to satisfy a woman. They are the perfect demographic for a cynical demagogue who does the impossible and makes libertarians look even more ridiculous.

Then there’s the delusional crew. These are good guys. They’ve come through for us in the past. They’d make good presidents. They’re just not going to make good presidents starting in January 2029, unless JD bows out for some reason, and Marco Rubio then bows out for some reason. That’s a lot of bowing, and it’s just not going to happen. I mean, it could happen. And they might come riding to the inauguration in a glittering silver carriage pulled by unicorns.

JD Vance is already taking some swipes at Ted Cruz and vice versa. I think Ted Cruz is a huge asset to the Republican Party. I did something for Ted Cruz that a guy like me — significantly Scottish — rarely does and gave him money the last time he ran for president, so I am speaking as a supporter. What I have to say as a supporter is this: Ted, buddy, you have zero chance of winning the nomination, so don’t waste our time and your dignity trying to win it in 2028. I know that Ted Cruz really, really wants to be president, and I think he’d make a good president, but over the next couple of cycles, a Ted Cruz presidency is the American political equivalent of “fetch.” It just ain’t going to happen.

John Kennedy is the senator from Louisiana who specializes in cornpone country-fried aphorisms and the surgical cross-examination of witnesses at committee hearings. Far from being some backward rube, this guy was a sensational trial lawyer (I read and appreciated his Louisiana Law Review pieces on products liability) and has made noises like he might give it a shot. OK, I like the guy. He’s doing a good job when he’s not going on weird, Trump-targeted tangents like pushing to outlaw naming buildings after living people five weeks before the midterms, but he doesn’t need to be president in 2028. Maybe somebody told him he’d have a shot, but he’s smart enough not to listen.

And there’s Brian Kemp from Georgia, who seems to think he’s got a shot. I don’t want to hear one damn thing about his presidential aspirations unless he delivers the governorship for Rick Jackson and the Senate seat for Mike Collins. And after that, I still don’t want to hear one damn thing about his presidential aspirations. He’s just not going to be president in 2028, and probably not ever.

Other good guys who get mentioned are Doug Burgum, Tom Cotton, Ron DeSantis, and several others. Again, all good guys. They all would make a terrific chief executive. But none of them is going to make a terrific chief executive next cycle. They should focus on doing the jobs that they’re doing. They can try again down the road.

With the emphasis on “down the road.” See, there’s a big roadblock in front of 2028. It’s Donald Trump, and he’s directing traffic on that figurative road. Right now, the only guy who’s driving through the barrier is JD Vance. You might not like it. You might not dig it. But that’s the way it is. And the sooner we all get that through our heads, the sooner we can start focusing on winning in 2028 — after we win in 2026, of course.

news.title: Trump Administration Ends EV Mandate; Consumers Benefit
news.text:
In a far-reaching move, on September 28, President Donald Trump’s Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) rescinded a rule enacted under President Biden to force drivers into electric vehicles.

As part of Biden’s “whole of government approach” to fight climate change, the EPA effectively banned whole classes of cars and trucks by imposing stronger fuel economy standards that would have been impossible to meet for most automobiles powered by internal combustion engines.

As written, Biden’s rule would have required vehicle fleets to get more than 50 miles per gallon (MPG) equivalent by 2031, up from the 30.1 MPG standard today. By the Biden EPA’s own estimate, the rule would effectively have required 26 percent in 2027, and 56 percent of new vehicles sold in 2032 to be EVs.

Yet, even with government subsidies for the purchase of EVs and for EV infrastructure like charging stations, currently, EVs only account for 7.3 percent of new car sales. EPA projected that the rescinded rule would have drastically reduced the availability of gasoline- and diesel-fueled cars and trucks, hybrids, and plug-in hybrids, which together currently make up 92.7 percent of the market, to just 29 percent of sales by 2032.

Aside from the loss of choice, the Biden rules would have increased the costs of remaining vehicles dramatically. EVs already cost thousands more than comparable fossil fuel-powered vehicles. That rule wouldn’t have made EVs cheaper, but it would have added thousands of dollars to the cost of new non-electric vehicles.

Trump’s action changes all that. It did not rescind CAFE standards entirely; he couldn’t do that if he wanted to because they are codified into law. So, EPA under Administrator Lee Zeldin dramatically reduced future increases in fuel economy standards, from 50.4 MPG by 2031 to 34.9 MPG.

This is a good start. It should maintain consumer choice concerning the types of features cars and trucks have and the types of vehicles sold. Under Trump’s rule, if fuel economy is not one’s most important factor when buying a new car or truck, they can still purchase an SUV, car, or truck.

Congress should never have gotten into the business of setting fuel economy standards. It was an inept attempt to reduce dependence on foreign oil, primarily from the Middle East, in response to the 1973 Arab oil embargo. The belief was that if you forced automakers to produce more fuel-efficient cars, people would use less gas, and oil imports would fall.

What happened was that automakers began to make fuel-efficient cars and ended production of certain types of vehicles that people liked, like muscle cars, station wagons, and hybrid trucks/cars. Those who purchased fuel-efficient cars wound up driving more miles because driving became cheaper, and a new class of vehicles was born: minivans and four-door trucks. Imported oil did not fall but rather increased, until nearly 40 years later during Trump’s first term when he took steps to expand production and put America on the path to energy dominance.

Station wagons virtually disappeared from the market, replaced by the newly created CAFE minivan, which was counted as a light truck with lower fuel economy standards. Truck appearances also dramatically changed, with two-door trucks declining and four-door trucks topping the sales charts virtually overnight, as people voted with their wallets for vehicles with power, utility, comfort, and amenities, regardless of fuel economy.

To the extent that fuel economy is a person’s prime consideration when they buy a vehicle, there are more than 40 models sold in the United States available today that get 40 mpg or more. Only two of those vehicles are in the Top 10 in sales. None of the vehicles that get more than 50 mpg are in the top 10 in sales. On the other hand, five of the top 10 are full-sized pickup trucks and three are SUVs or crossovers.

Worse than the government substituting its judgment of what people should care about when they choose a vehicle was the fact that the government’s CAFE standards wound up killing people. To improve fuel economy, automakers primarily reduced the size and weight of vehicles. Unfortunately, this downsizing had tragic consequences. Since the laws of physics have not changed, by putting more people in smaller, lighter vehicles, at least tens of thousands of people have been put at risk of injury and death each time CAFE standards are increased.

For example, the National Academy of Sciences estimated 1,300 to 2,600 additional deaths per year were caused by vehicle downsizing. Research by Harvard and the Brookings Institution put that figure higher still, estimating that every 100-pound weight reduction adds 2,200 to 3,900 fatalities per model year over a decade of driving. Whereas the Competitive Enterprise Institute attributed 2,600 to 4,500 deaths each year to fleet weight limits. Over the decades of its existence, the CAFE mandates have killed more Americans than all wars from Vietnam to the present combined.

As a result, by slowing, and one might hope, ending future CAFE standard increases, the Trump administration is not just saving consumers dollars and choices, but it is literally saving lives. Thanks, President Trump, for putting Americans’ freedom of choice and lives first.

H. Sterling Burnett, Ph.D. (hsburnett@heartland.org) is the Director of the Arthur B. Robinson Center on Climate and Environmental Policy at The Heartland Institute, a nonpartisan, non-profit research organization based in Illinois.

news.title: The Anti-Trump Media and 'Economic Pessimism'
news.text:
In a college psychology course, my class studied an experiment.

This is an oversimplification, but the experiment went as follows. A group of college students was shown a paper on which a six-inch line was drawn. The paper was passed to the students sitting around the table. They were asked to estimate the length of the line. Now, this experiment was rigged. The instructor and all but one of the students were told to say, "About three inches." Again, the line was clearly longer than three inches.

The point was to determine whether these obviously wrong guesses would cause the unsuspecting student — the one not in on the scheme and the last one at the table to offer a guess — to also say, "About three inches." In the overwhelming majority of cases, the unsuspecting students also said, "About three inches."

Now there are a few ways to look at this. But one explanation is that the consensus, though clearly wrong, altered the way the final student viewed the length of the line, as in, "If everybody sees it that way, I must be wrong."

How much of current pessimism about the economy is driven by what the media tells us about the economy and how we should feel about it?

For example, the standard common definition of a recession is back-to-back quarters of negative economic growth. In 2025, the first year of President Donald Trump's second term, every quarter after revisions had positive economic growth. So far this year, each quarter had seen positive economic growth.

But a July 2026 Economist/YouGov poll found that 41 percent of adult Americans believed the country was in a recession, with Democrats three times more likely than Republicans to feel this way. A Napolitan News Service/Rasmussen poll conducted at the end of September 2026 found that 39 percent of registered voters believed the country was in a recession.

Consider the media coverage of the economy the month before the presidential election of 1992, when President George H.W. Bush ran against Arkansas Gov. Bill Clinton. There had been 19 months of positive economic growth leading up to October 1992. A Gallup poll, however, found that a majority of Americans thought the economy was in a recession.

Investor's Business Daily noted that in October 1992, 90 percent of the economic news in newspapers was negative. The election was held on Nov. 3. Clinton won, and that month only 14 percent of the economic news in newspapers was negative. As to the ABC, NBC and CBS nightly news, about 90 percent of the news about the economy was negative. After the election, for the remaining two months of the year, 60 percent of the economic news in the same newscasts was positive.

Yes, gas prices since the start of the Iran War have gone up. But at 2.5 percent of income, the amount Americans spend on gas is less than during the gas spikes of the 1970s. And Americans drive twice as far on a gallon of gas compared to the 1970s.

The average income is at an all-time high. The percentage of those living in poverty is at an all-time low. The stock market indices have hit record highs, and 401(k)s have seen large increases.

Consumers are spending. People who fear an economic downturn and who fear the loss of their jobs typically do not spend the way consumers have been doing in recent months. The Atlanta Fed's GDPNow model estimates a third-quarter 2026 growth of 3.7 percent.

The Media Research Center found the Big 3 nightly news coverage of Trump was negative in both terms.

"News aggregators" like Microsoft, Apple, Google, Yahoo, TikTok and YouTube are where Americans now primarily get their news. In 2025, Google curated 73 percent of articles from outlets with a bias to the left — and just one percent of articles from outlets biased to the right. For all the aggregators, less than 10 percent of their curated articles came from outlets on the right.

In "Lessons from the Recession: A Management and Communication Perspective," published in 1997, the authors write: "... the highly negative view of the economy in 1992 was due in large part to widespread misperceptions about its performance and prospects, and that unduly negative coverage on network television played some major role informing those misperceptions."

The anti-Trump media clearly influences how people think and feel about the economy. The only question is to what degree.

Larry Elder is a bestselling author and nationally syndicated radio talk show host.

news.title: Who’s beefing up among big cattle countries
news.text:
Reading Time: 3 minutes

As this red meat market cycle extends over a year, and memories of past seasons become hazy, it’s easy to forget how ridiculously high prices have become for both lambs and cattle. 

Much of this surge in pricing has been a direct result of red meat shortages in key markets. The United States and Canadian cow herds were hammered by drought in 2022 and early 2023. Australian sheep farmers were dealt the same hand in 2024 and early 2025, all while the European Union and United Kingdom have continued to report fundamental declines in their beef cow herds and ewe breeding flocks.

Now feels like a fitting time to assess what the forward outlook is for key global markets in terms of supplies – more of the same, or are changes ahead?

In the US, herd rebuilding continues to occur at a much slower pace than previously expected. High livestock values and patchy drought conditions have meant more potential breeding cattle have been sent to processors than once expected. 

US President Donald Trump’s erratic tinkering in the beef market has not earned him many friends among ranchers either, and this uncertainty is also discouraging rebuilding.

With that said, there are early signs that cattle numbers are near the bottom and will slowly climb. Heifers are the smallest portion of the steer/heifer kill in nine years, while the beef cow kill (that is, excluding dairy cows) is lowest relative to the total herd size since peak herd rebuilding in 2015. This should see US cattle production start to noticeably increase from 2028 onwards. 

Australia’s cattle industry has been one of the few at the top of its game. It has exported an unprecedented volume of beef this year, more than last year’s record highs and already above 15 of the past 20 full calendar years. 

It was expected that the lure of big dollars would cause more culling of the Australian breeding herd and noticeably slow production next year. However, next year’s slaughter forecast has been revised upwards to match 2025’s level, to only 2% less than this year.

The lack of significant drought this past year plus the continued expansion of feedlots – which are killing around a million more cattle per year than normal – have shortened the time to finished cattle. This has freed up paddock space for breeding cattle to a greater degree than first thought. 

And, if anything, El Niño drought has the potential to push next year’s kill even higher, especially in early months.

Another major beef country set to come off its peak is Brazil. Its 12-month cattle kill has historically ranged between 55 million and 65 million head, but it surged to a record high of 86 million last year. 

While there’s been fundamental growth in the Brazilian herd, around two-thirds of the jump in their cattle slaughter in the past two years has been due to more cows and heifers entering the slaughter system. 

In the 12 months to the end of June, these made up 47% of the total kill, a record high since data collection began in 2000. This has eaten into breeding cattle numbers, and it’s therefore expected that Brazilian cattle production will decline next year and likely the years following too.

Chinese cattle production flies under the radar as almost all its beef is consumed domestically, but the volumes it produces are significant, accounting for around 70% of total consumption in the country. 

According to US Department of Agriculture data, in 2024 China’s total cattle numbers rose to an 18-year high. These high numbers, combined with large imported beef volumes, weakened cattle prices to unprofitable levels. This led to widespread culling last year, generating record-high beef production, which sparked China’s investigation into beef imports and subsequent quota limits. 

With the cattle herd now in recovery mode, the USDA forecasts China’s beef production next year to fall to the lowest level since 2018, down 16% from last year’s peak.
news.summary:
From El Niño to long-term herd plans, now is a good time for an audit of global trends and outlooks.

news.title: The American Presidency’s Missing Guardrails
news.text:
The United States is a wonderful country with enduring traditions, powerful institutions and a strong practical constitution. Yet that system contains a dangerous contradiction. It gives one individual command of the world’s most powerful military and sole authority to authorize nuclear force, but demands almost nothing about physical, mental or moral fitness beyond age, citizenship and residency.

The president is the face of the nation and an example whom millions admire, imitate and defend. Conduct affecting only a few people when committed by an ordinary citizen can reshape national standards when excused in the White House. If dishonesty, sexual misconduct or contempt for law is tolerated in the president, followers may conclude that the same behaviour is acceptable.

Bill Clinton’s relationship with White House intern Monica Lewinsky demonstrated this danger. The issue was not confined to whether a relationship between adults was criminal. The president conducted it with a young subordinate inside the institution representing American dignity, then gave false and misleading testimony in the Paula Jones lawsuit. Clinton was impeached but acquitted and completed his term. He was later held in civil contempt, accepted a five-year suspension of his law licence and paid financial penalties. An ordinary citizen who lied under oath or obstructed justice could face prosecution and imprisonment; presidential power converted Clinton’s misconduct into a partisan argument over removal.

Extraordinary ideas are often introduced as jokes or trial balloons, then repeated until resistance weakens.

Donald Trump presents a broader test. His social relationship with Jeffrey Epstein is documented through photographs, statements and travel records. A prosecutor’s email released by the Justice Department said Trump flew on Epstein’s aircraft eight times during the 1990s. The releases also contain grave allegations that Trump denies and that remain unproven. Appearance in a file is not proof of crime, but it does not end the constitutional question.

When allegations concern the president, agencies holding the evidence are led by his appointees within an executive branch he controls. Even honest officials operate under an unavoidable conflict of interest, while citizens may fear that evidence can be delayed, discredited or withheld. The answer is neither automatic conviction nor blind acceptance of presidential denials, but investigation structurally independent of the president. Trump’s adjudicated cases make the problem clearer. A civil jury found him liable for sexually abusing and defaming E. Jean Carroll. A New York jury convicted him on 34 felony counts of falsifying business records, although his appeal continues. He nevertheless returned to the presidency.

Richard Nixon participated in the Watergate cover-up, resigned and received a pardon preventing federal prosecution. Warren Harding’s affairs and hush-money arrangements became public while corruption surrounded his administration. These cases show how party loyalty and executive power separate presidential consequences from those confronting ordinary citizens.

Physical and mental incapacity reveal the same institutional weakness. James Garfield performed almost no official work for 79 days after being shot, while the government operated largely on autopilot.

Grover Cleveland secretly underwent cancer surgery without informing his vice president or most of his Cabinet. Woodrow Wilson remained president after a devastating stroke left him partially paralyzed and isolated, while his wife, physician and secretary controlled access to him. Franklin Roosevelt’s grave cardiovascular condition was concealed while he sought a fourth term. The Twenty-Fifth Amendment improved the Constitution but did not eliminate the conflict. Its involuntary mechanism depends upon the vice president and Cabinet—political associates and appointees—declaring the president unable to serve.

Section Four has never been invoked. Joe Biden’s visible decline became politically undeniable during the 2024 campaign, yet party pressure, not an independent examination, ended his campaign. Trump’s rambling speeches about Iranian “drug factories” and Iran “taking out” Los Angeles and San Diego similarly demand transparent examination rather than reassurance from his staff. The impeachment mechanism is equally vulnerable to party loyalty. Removal requires a two-thirds Senate vote. Andrew Johnson escaped conviction by one vote. Clinton was acquitted. Trump was impeached twice and acquitted twice, even when 57 senators supported conviction after January 6. A president protected by a sufficiently loyal party can therefore survive evidence or conduct that would end the career of almost any ordinary public employee.

Trump’s references to a third term must be treated seriously. Extraordinary ideas are often introduced as jokes or trial balloons, then repeated until resistance weakens. If Republicans hypothetically secured two-thirds of both houses, Trump would not hesitate to propose an amendment creating a third-term route, perhaps by distinguishing consecutive from nonconsecutive terms. Ratification by three-fourths of the states would remain necessary, but the Twenty-Second Amendment must be actively defended.

America’s system also displays great strength. Local democracy can protect an amplified azan under the same rules governing church bells and other religious announcements. Voters can elect leaders such as New York Mayor Zohran Mamdani and nominate Michigan Senate candidate Abdul El-Sayed despite intense religious and political opposition. Administrations can reverse policies through elections, allowing democratic correction far more quickly than a hereditary monarchy. These achievements demonstrate that reforming presidential accountability would strengthen, not weaken, the constitutional order.

The country needs an independent Presidential Integrity and Capacity Commission established by constitutional amendment. Its existence, authority and independence must derive directly from the Constitution, with protected funding, secure tenure and enforceable investigative powers. Neither the president nor a congressional majority should be able to dissolve it, dismiss its investigators or prevent it from carrying out its constitutional duties.

The commission should include judges, physicians and constitutional experts, selected through a balanced appointment process that prevents domination by any president or political party. Its mandate should cover presidential capacity, serious dishonesty under oath, corruption and abuse of office, and serious criminal misconduct, including sexual abuse and obstruction of justice. It should conduct regular assessments of capacity and investigate credible, evidence-supported allegations within these defined areas. It must not become a morality police empowered to punish unpopular opinions, political disagreements or ordinary human failings. The commission should preserve evidence, publish substantiated findings with appropriate protections for victims and sensitive information, and submit its evidence to the House of Representatives and the Senate. The House would determine whether to impeach, and the Senate would determine whether to convict and remove. Findings of incapacity should follow a separately defined constitutional procedure, because inability to perform presidential duties is distinct from impeachable misconduct. Yet independent evidence gathering alone cannot resolve the danger of partisan protection. A congressional majority may refuse to act even when compelling evidence exists. If the proposed reform is intended to prevent that failure from leaving a president beyond effective accountability, the amendment must expressly establish an additional, narrowly defined judicial mechanism.

That mechanism should permit an independent constitutional tribunal to hear qualifying cases and order the remedies—including suspension or removal—specifically authorized by the amendment, under rigorous evidentiary standards and with a right of review. Such authority cannot be assumed merely because the commission operates under judicial oversight. At the same time, the amendment must prohibit presidential interference with investigators, destruction or suppression of records, and self-pardons for conduct under examination. Presidential power must never become a shield that prevents evidence from being discovered or accountability from taking place.

The presidency magnifies character. A president’s words and conduct influence the ethical atmosphere of the entire country, legitimize behaviour for followers and shape how the world understands America. This higher standard is not an attack on democratic choice; it protects voters from deception and prevents temporary occupants of office from using public power to conceal private wrongdoing or incapacity. The republic therefore cannot demand less integrity from its most powerful citizen than it demands from everyone else. The president must be not only legally qualified to occupy the office, but physically capable, mentally sound and morally worthy of the example the office inevitably creates.

The writer is a former press secretary to the president; former press minister to the Embassy of Pakistan to France and former MD (SRBC).

news.title: Tropical Storm Isaias forecast to hit U.S. Gulf Coast as hurricane
news.text:
Tropical Storm Isaias formed in the Gulf of Mexico today and is forecast to strengthen into a hurricane before slamming into the southern U.S. coast early on Saturday, bringing heavy rains, storm surges, and possible tornadoes across several states, the National Hurricane Center said.

The storm is expected to pass through areas with significant offshore oil and gas production, along with onshore refining facilities, which could pressure inventories and already-high prices at the pump.

Michael Brennan, director of the NHC, said in a video briefing today that Isaias could be a “major” hurricane — Category 3 or higher — when it makes landfall and could have “multiple, life-threatening impacts from storm surge, heavy rainfall flooding and hurricane force winds.”

Isaias would be the first hurricane of the season in the Atlantic, according to the NHC, and could tie the record for the latest first Atlantic hurricane with one that hit on October 8, 1905. The strong El Nino weather pattern this year has suppressed Atlantic hurricane development by increasing vertical wind shear, which disrupts the formation of strengthening tropical storms.

About 11.2 million barrels of oil production could be lost across the Gulf through the duration of the storm, a marked increase from the 7.1 million barrels impacted by Tropical Storm Bertha in July, according to a model forecast from consulting firm Earth Science Associates.

The NHC expects Isaias to develop into a hurricane by Thursday as it quickly picks up power over the warm Gulf waters before making landfall early on Saturday, most likely somewhere along the Mississippi, Alabama or Florida panhandle coast. The storm was located about 500 miles (805 km) south of the Louisiana coast early today.

Isaias could produce isolated rainfall amounts of 10 inches across parts of the Gulf Coast, stretching from Louisiana to the Florida Panhandle, the NHC said in its latest bulletin.

Tornadoes are possible in the rainbands of Isaias across the Florida Panhandle and Alabama from Friday evening through Saturday, with more tornadoes expected further inland as the storm moves north.

The storm could also produce 3 inches or more of rain further inland, with the NHC warning that “flash and urban flooding, along with isolated river flooding, will be possible” across the Southeast.

Isaias is expected to run into strong upper-level winds, known as vertical wind shear, in the final 24 hours before it reaches the northern Gulf Coast, which could weaken the storm.

Still, the NHC says it is “looking more likely that Isaias will be a significant hurricane when it reaches the coast.”

Florida Governor Ron DeSantis on Tuesday had already declared a state of emergency for portions of the state. Some officials across the region were urging residents to voluntarily evacuate.

Florida U.S. Senator Rick Scott wrote on social media that he had spoken with President Donald Trump about the storm, and that “the federal government is going to show up for Florida and make sure we have everything needed to prepare, respond, and recover.”

The Marine Minerals Administration, which monitors offshore oil and gas operators in the Gulf of Mexico, said today that personnel have been evacuated from eight production platforms and two non-dynamically positioned ahead of the storm.

About 25% of current oil production in the Gulf, or 511,619 barrels of oil per day, has been shut in, the agency said, citing operator reports. Just over 350 million cubic feet per day of natural gas production has also been shut in, or about 16.4% of total output from the region.

The companies with the most exposure to the storm include BP , Chevron, ENI, Murphy Oil and Shell

Additional reporting by Sukanya Mitra in Bengaluru and Costas Pitas in Los Angeles.
news.summary: Tropical Storm Isaias formed in the Gulf of Mexico today and is forecast to strengthen into a hurricane before slamming into the southern U.S. coast early on Saturday, bringing heavy rains, storm surges, and possible tornadoes across several states, the National Hurricane Center said.

news.title: Trump proposes Camp David-style presidential retreat at his private Florida golf club
news.text:
FORT LAUDERDALE, Fla. (AP) — President Donald Trump on Wednesday said he wants to develop one of his Florida golf courses into a presidential retreat where his successors can spend quiet weekends on the greens, describing it as “sort of a Camp David ” that he says would already have many of the security features needed to host presidents and world leaders.

The proposal for the retreat on Trump’s private golf course in West Palm Beach would comingle the presidency with Trump’s business ventures beyond his time in office, and is the the latest example of Trump seeking ways to leave his imprint on the presidency.

“It’s a great idea, and it’ll be used a lot,” Trump said, claiming it was suggested by the United States Secret Service. “It seems that all presidents play golf.”

The plan has already been submitted to local officials. Trump, an avid golfer, rattled off the benefits of the property a short drive from his Mar-a-Lago home during an unrelated event in the Oval Office, noting that it’s close to an airport and has some distance from residential homes and tall buildings, which pose security risks.

He did not mention that the golf course was the site of an unsuccessful attempt on his life in 2024. Trump was playing at the Trump International Golf Club during a break from the campaign trail when a Secret Service agent spotted an armed man in the trees lining the club’s perimeter fence. The man was arrested after a chase and later convicted of trying to kill Trump, and was sentenced to life in prison.

Past presidents have used Camp David, a rustic compound in Maryland, as a weekend retreat and a place to host presidential meetings. Trump has spent less time there, often opting for his own properties, including golf clubs in Florida, New Jersey and Virginia.

Palm Beach County sees what it calls a ‘historic opportunity’

Trump’s proposal follows other projects by the lifelong real estate developer to build a White House ballroom, gild the Oval Office, erect a triumphal arch, renovate the Kennedy Center, refurbish the Lincoln Memorial Reflecting Pool and rebuild a golf course in East Potomac Park. He has also begun planning a future presidential library in a Miami skyscraper.

In a letter to Palm Beach County commissioners last month, first reported by the Palm Beach Post, an attorney who represents the golf course said Trump is offering to designate it as a “U.S. Presidential Golf Course.”

“Just as Camp David, Windsor Castle, or the Elysée Palace are known worldwide, so too will the Presidential Golf Course in Palm Beach County,” Harvey Oyer said in the letter.

Palm Beach County Administrator Joseph Abruzzo said in a statement that local officials are eager to explore what this “historic opportunity” could mean to the community. “This likely would further cement Palm Beach County’s place on the national and international stage for generations to come,” Abruzzo said.

Oyer’s letter said the West Palm Beach golf course could be used by current and former presidents, along with visiting foreign heads of state. The Trump Organization owns the golf club but leases the land from the county, which would need to approve any changes.

Under the proposal, the club would pay to build a new presidential lodging and then work with the Secret Service and other agencies to provide free access to the federal government. The retreat would have a separate entrance from the private club, which earned Trump nearly $37 million during his first year back in office, according to his financial disclosure.

“This is a gift that the President would like to share with his successors, the people of America, and his fellow Palm Beach County residents,” Oyer wrote. “It should be noted that President Trump will be out of office before this proposed project could be completed so this is a gift to his successors.”

Oyer highlighted past U.S. presidents who turned over land for public use. Dwight Eisenhower donated his Gettysburg Farm in Pennsylvania to the National Park Service, and Franklin D. Roosevelt donated part of his estate in Hyde Park, New York.

Years before it was bought by Trump, Mar-a-Lago itself was proposed as a “Winter White House.”

Businesswoman and socialite Marjorie Merriweather Post left the home to the National Park Service when she died in 1973, but the agency returned the home to her estate in 1980 because of high maintenance costs. Trump bought the property in 1985, and it later became his primary residence.

news.text:

Potential combat operations include massive bombing campaigns targeting Iranian energy, infrastructure and nuclear facilities, according to the sources.

He made the remarks in an interview with the semi-official Fars news agency, which was published on Wednesday, while stressing that Iranian armed forces had previously launched such operations against the "enemy".

He noted among the operations carried out by the Iranian armed forces based on the new doctrine were a missile strike against a US base in Jordan in late July, as well as several missile and drone attacks over the past months against the bases of the "counter-revolutionary and separatist" groups stationed in Iraq's semi-autonomous Kurdistan region.

He added the strike against the US base, which was preemptive, "wrested the initiative from them and left them unable to take any action."

Akraminia stressed that carrying out preemptive operations while adhering to principles, such as necessity, urgency, and proportionality, is considered "legitimate."

news.title: Rubio blasts globalism and open borders at birthplace of Western civilization (VIDEO)
news.text:
US Secretary of State Marco Rubio has delivered a blistering attack on open borders, globalism and the erosion of national sovereignty in Europe, warning from the ancient heart of Athens that the West risks sliding into “atrophy, servitude and decline.”

Speaking on Wednesday from the Pnyx, the ancient assembly site beneath the Acropolis, Rubio argued that Western governments had spent decades dismantling the very principles that made their civilization successful.

“‘Nationalism’ became a dirty word,” Rubio said. “So we tore down our monuments, we condemned our own history, and in too many places we taught our children to be ashamed of the countries they would inherit.”

“In the process we opened our borders, and outsourced our industry, and allowed our militaries to wither and to decay,” he added.

Rubio contrasted the globalist approach embraced by much of the European political establishment with the Trump administration’s “America First” doctrine, arguing that governments have an obligation to put their own citizens above international institutions.

“It has become fashionable today to believe that enlightened foreign policy means prioritizing the global community over one’s own people,” he said, insisting the ancient Greeks understood that there was “nothing selfish or wrong about loyalty to your nation” or defending its interests “above all else.”

The remarks amount to the latest broadside from Washington in an increasingly bitter ideological dispute with the EU over migration, censorship and national sovereignty. The Trump administration has repeatedly portrayed Brussels and Western European governments as having betrayed their own populations.

Vice President JD Vance has previously warned that Europe risks committing “civilizational suicide” through uncontrolled migration and curbs on free expression. At the Munich Security Conference last year, he argued that the continent’s greatest danger came not from Russia or China, but from an internal retreat from democratic values. The administration formalized much of that critique in its 2025 National Security Strategy, which warned that Europe faces potential “civilizational erasure.”

The transatlantic clash has become particularly visible over immigration. Just this week, President Donald Trump blamed violent unrest in France on “out of control mass migration,” rejecting claims that the nationwide student protests were primarily about underfunded schools. US Ambassador to the UN Mike Waltz similarly blamed Europe’s “open borders” and “unchecked immigration” for growing public anger.

Rubio nevertheless stopped short of calling for a rupture with Europe. Instead, he urged the continent to follow Washington’s nationalist turn, praising Greece as a “model ally” and saying there were already signs of a broader shift.

“We believe that Europe can awaken from its long slumber and rekindle the fire that was lit here millennia ago,” he said.

Rubio declared that the US, under Trump, had already chosen the “unapologetic pursuit of national power,” including reindustrialization, securing critical supply chains, rebuilding the military and seeking dominance in artificial intelligence, advanced manufacturing, weapons, space and other strategic industries.

The West, he warned, is now at an “inflection point,” with decisions made over the next decade potentially determining whether it remains at the center of global power or accepts a future of decline.

news.title: Iran will never have nuclear weapon, says Marco Rubio
news.text:
Washington, Oct 8 (SocialNews.XYZ) US Secretary of State Marco Rubio has declared that Iran will never be allowed to acquire nuclear weapons under President Donald Trump, accusing Tehran of building a massive missile and drone arsenal to shield its nuclear ambitions from international military action.

Speaking at a joint press conference with Greek Foreign Minister Giorgos Gerapetritis in Athens, Rubio said Washington's position remained firm despite questions about whether the United States might accept limited uranium enrichment by Iran under a future agreement.

"Iran cannot have a nuclear weapon, simple, period and end of story," Rubio said.

He declined to specify what level of nuclear activity Washington might accept in negotiations, but made clear that preventing Iran from developing nuclear weapons remained the administration's central objective.

"Anything they agree to that would be acceptable to the United States has to be something that ensures that Iran will never have a nuclear weapon," he said.

Rubio was responding to a question about remarks by Vice President JD Vance suggesting that Iran needed to take meaningful action concerning its nuclear enrichment capacity.

The Secretary of State argued that Tehran had sought to develop overwhelming conventional military strength to deter attacks on its nuclear facilities.

According to Rubio, Iran's strategy was to accumulate sufficient missiles and drones to threaten devastating retaliation against countries attempting to stop its nuclear programme.

He said the Trump administration had acted to prevent Iran from reaching that position.

"He destroyed their drone program, their drone manufacturing capability," Rubio said, referring to Trump.

"He destroyed their missile capability. He severely eroded both of those capabilities in terms of current launchers. He destroyed their navy. He destroyed their air force."

These claims about the extent of the damage to Iran's military capabilities were not independently substantiated during the press conference.

Rubio maintained that Iran's military position had deteriorated considerably and that Tehran could no longer rely on its conventional forces to deter action against its nuclear activities.

"They will never have a nuclear weapon, period, not as long as President Trump is in office," he said.

The Secretary of State also delivered a bleak assessment of Iran's economic prospects, blaming its leadership for the country's worsening financial difficulties.

He said international sanctions were placing enormous pressure on Tehran and predicted further deterioration in the Iranian economy.

news.title: Democrats sue US President Trump over taxpayer-funded ad campaign  - Guyana Inquirer – Daily Guyana News
news.text:
The Democratic National Committee has filed a lawsuit against United States President Donald Trump over television advertisements that were publicly funded and allegedly used to promote his political policies.

Ken Martin, who heads the Democratic Party’s leadership body, suggested in a statement on Wednesday that the ads were designed to bolster Republican odds in the upcoming November 3 midterm elections.

“Donald Trump is misusing millions of taxpayer dollars to fund pure propaganda ads in a last-ditch attempt to save Republicans in November,” Martin said.

A second lawsuit was filed later in the day over the same set of ads by Common Cause, a democracy watchdog group.

It argued that the ads were “overtly political” and therefore ran afoul of laws that bar public funds from being used for political propaganda.

“These ads are not public-service announcements,” Common Cause said in its lawsuit, citing a justification Trump has offered for the television spots. “They are personal publicity and political propaganda through and through.”

Both lawsuits argue that, to create the ad campaign, Trump directed the White House to repurpose $20m in funds that Congress allocated for commemorative activities related to border security, including for those killed in the line of duty.

That manoeuvre, they argue, violates the separation of powers established in the US Constitution.

“The founders made clear more than 200 years ago that the executive can spend money only according to Congress’s direction,” Common Cause’s lawsuit said.

The two lawsuits also point to a provision Congress includes in its appropriation bills barring the use of taxpayer funds for “publicity or propaganda purposes”.

Both complaints seek to have the ads to be declared illegal and for the expenditures to be stopped. They also pushed for steps to be taken to recover any money already spent on the ads.

The Democrats’ lawsuit was filed in Washington, DC, while the Common Cause complaint will be heard in the southern district of New York.

Trump has faced mounting criticism over the ads, which began airing in September.

So far, the advertising campaign has cost more than $12m to run, according to the media tracking firm AdImpact.

The $20m Trump tapped for the ads comes from a $175m package Congress assigned to the Department of Homeland Security as part of Trump’s immigration enforcement agenda.

Critics have pointed out that one of the ads appears nearly identical to a television spot Trump used in his re-election campaign in 2024.

Three ads have aired so far. In one, a choir sings “love me” over a montage of Trump as he declares the US will “never be a communist country”. Another uses images of Mount Rushmore as Trump heralds a new “golden age of America”.

The third is darker: Trump walks towards the camera in black and white, warning of a “final battle” against the “deep state” and other perceived enemies.

On Wednesday, the news agency Reuters and the research firm Ipsos released a poll showing the ads are highly unpopular. Some 86 percent of the Americans surveyed, including four out of five Republicans, said it was inappropriate for Trump to have used public money for them.

Trump has defended the ads as “promotion for the country”, and he has argued they were similar to public outreach campaigns put out by previous administrations.

But after a bipartisan backlash, Trump said on Monday that he would start paying for future ads himself instead of using public funds.

He did not, however, commit to paying back the money already spent on the existing ads.

Members of Trump’s Republican Party have been among those speaking out against the ad campaign.

Senator Thom Tillis, a Republican from North Carolina, said the advertisements resembled something former Hungarian leader Viktor Orban would put out.

Senate Majority Leader John Thune, meanwhile, indicated he agreed with the message in one of the advertisements, but he emphasised that “it shouldn’t be paid for with taxpayer dollars”.

news.text:

The President said more than 1.4 million beneficiaries in Texas would be covered.

He did not provide a detailed breakdown of the funding, eligibility criteria or the mechanism through which the payments would be made.

Trump presented the Medicare and healthcare payments as part of a wider effort to return money to American households.

He also promised a $5,000 payment to every adult American citizen if Republicans retained control of both chambers of Congress in November.

The question referred to healthcare refunds, payments to seniors and the proposed $5,000 dividend.

Trump defended the measures, arguing that economic growth and tariff revenues had made them possible.

"Well, what we're doing is we have tremendous growth," he said.

news.title: US forms high-level task force to regulate AI superintelligence
news.text:
Washington, Oct 8 (SocialNews.XYZ) The United States has established a high-level task force to shape its approach to artificial intelligence superintelligence, Secretary of State Marco Rubio has said, acknowledging that the rapidly advancing technology could deliver enormous benefits while also posing serious risks that governments must address.

Speaking at a joint press conference with Greek Foreign Minister Giorgos Gerapetritis in Athens, Rubio said the Trump administration had begun developing a framework to determine how Washington should respond to the opportunities and dangers associated with increasingly powerful artificial intelligence systems.

The task force is being chaired by Jay Clayton and will examine potential regulatory measures, safeguards and ways to maximise the technology's economic and strategic benefits, he said.

"The US government has set up a process," Rubio said.

He explained that the administration wanted to understand both the potential advantages of superintelligence and the dangers that could arise from its development.

Rubio was responding to a question about the government's responsibility to prevent advanced AI laboratories from developing systems that could threaten humanity.

He said the administration had already assembled a group to consider these questions and develop an appropriate government response.

The Secretary of State described artificial intelligence as a rapidly evolving challenge requiring cooperation between governments and international partners.

"This is a new issue," Rubio said, before clarifying that the technology itself was not new but that public and government awareness of its implications had changed significantly.

He said Washington intended to work closely with allies as it developed its approach.

Rubio also referred to a recent gathering of technology leaders convened by President Donald Trump, saying a joint declaration had outlined broad principles for addressing superintelligence.

The administration's objective, he explained, was to encourage beneficial applications while limiting potential harm.

"How do we take the positives of it and harness it in a way that serves the interests of our country, and how do we mitigate or prevent the dangers of it?" Rubio said.

He said policymakers needed to understand the potential benefits and disadvantages before deciding what role government regulation should play.

Rubio stressed that the process had to move quickly because the technology was advancing at extraordinary speed.

The discussion also exposed the challenges facing governments seeking to regulate artificial intelligence without obstructing innovation.

Gerapetritis described AI as a major scientific and industrial breakthrough capable of transforming education, expanding knowledge and reducing gaps in expertise.

But he warned that the technology could also deepen inequalities and threaten democratic institutions.

The Greek minister identified misinformation, disinformation and addiction among vulnerable populations as areas requiring particular attention.

He argued that governments needed effective safeguards while recognising the difficulty of imposing regulatory limits on technological innovation.

"Our reality is that artificial intelligence is dual-use. It might be beneficial, but it can also be destructive," Gerapetritis said.

He called for a balanced approach that would protect citizens while allowing societies to benefit from technological advances.

"So yes to regulation, yes to technology, not no to technophobia," he said.

The exchange highlighted the growing international debate over the governance of advanced AI systems, particularly as governments consider how to manage technologies whose capabilities are developing faster than existing regulatory structures.
